description: The physics and engineering of mobile radio: from the generations of cellular standards through channel models, cellular design, digital modulation and coding in fading channels, multiple antennas and OFDM, and multiple access, with every link simulated and its error rate measured. Taught to the depth of a leading wireless communications course.
modelledOn: Rappaport, Wireless Communications: Principles and Practice
Tse and Viswanath, Fundamentals of Wireless Communication
outcomes: Trace the evolution from 1G to 5G and explain the architecture and key technologies of each generation.
Model path loss, shadowing and multipath fading and classify channels as narrowband or wideband, slow or fast.
Design a cellular layout with frequency reuse and compute signal-to-interference ratio, capacity and trunking performance.
Derive error probabilities for digital modulation in AWGN and fading channels and simulate them.
Explain channel coding, diversity, MIMO and OFDM and quantify their gains.
Compare TDMA, FDMA, CDMA and OFDMA and simulate a complete wireless link in MATLAB or Python.

units.title: Wireless communication systems and standards
topics: History: from Marconi to 5G; 1G AMPS, 2G GSM and IS-95, 2.5G GPRS/EDGE, 3G UMTS/CDMA2000, 4G LTE, 5G NR and what 6G research targets
Cellular network architecture: mobiles, base stations, core network, handover, roaming, SIM and authentication
Spectrum: allocation, licensing, Ghana's NCA bands, unlicensed bands (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, LoRa)
Other wireless systems: satellite, WLAN, WPAN, microwave links; coverage in rural Ghana
Simulation environment: MATLAB or Python with NumPy and SciPy

units.title: Modulation schemes and the radio link
topics: Analog modulation review: AM, FM; the transmitter and receiver chain; mixers, filters, amplifiers
Digital modulation overview: ASK, FSK, PSK, QAM; bandwidth efficiency and power efficiency
Pulse shaping, intersymbol interference, raised-cosine filters, eye diagrams
Link budget: transmit power, antenna gain, path loss, noise figure, receiver sensitivity

units.title: Statistical channel models: narrowband and wideband fading
topics: Large-scale propagation: free space, two-ray, log-distance path loss, empirical models (Okumura-Hata, COST 231); log-normal shadowing
Small-scale multipath: delay spread, coherence bandwidth, Doppler spread, coherence time
Narrowband fading: Rayleigh and Rician distributions; level crossing rate and fade duration
Wideband channels: tapped delay line models, power delay profile, frequency-selective fading
Classifying channels: flat versus frequency selective, slow versus fast; simulating Rayleigh fading (Jakes model)

units.title: Cellular concepts and system design
topics: The cellular concept: cells, clusters, frequency reuse, reuse distance and the cluster size
Co-channel and adjacent-channel interference; signal-to-interference ratio versus cluster size
Capacity: channels per cell, spectral efficiency; improving capacity with sectoring, cell splitting, microcells
Handover strategies, power control, mobility management
Designing a cellular layout for a Ghanaian town with given traffic and coverage targets

units.title: Quality of service and trunking
topics: Traffic theory: Erlangs, offered load, grade of service
Erlang B and Erlang C formulas; blocked-calls-cleared versus queued systems; trunking efficiency
QoS parameters for voice, data and video; delay, jitter, loss; scheduling in LTE
Dimensioning a cell's channels for a target blocking probability

units.title: Digital modulation and detection in AWGN; error probabilities
topics: Signal space representation; matched filter and correlation receivers; maximum likelihood detection
Error probabilities in AWGN for BPSK, QPSK, M-PSK, M-QAM, FSK; the Q-function and union bound
Performance in fading: average BER in Rayleigh fading and the diversity order; outage probability
Synchronisation and channel estimation in brief
Monte Carlo BER simulation and comparison with theory

units.title: Coding for wireless channels
topics: Channel capacity (Shannon) for AWGN and fading channels; coding gain
Block codes (Hamming, Reed-Solomon), convolutional codes and Viterbi decoding; interleaving against bursts
Turbo codes, LDPC and polar codes as used in 3G, 4G and 5G
Hybrid ARQ and adaptive modulation and coding

units.title: Multiple antenna systems: diversity, MIMO, OFDM
topics: Diversity: time, frequency, space; selection, equal-gain and maximal-ratio combining
MIMO: spatial multiplexing, capacity scaling, space-time codes (Alamouti), beamforming, massive MIMO in 5G
OFDM: orthogonal subcarriers, IFFT/FFT implementation, cyclic prefix, PAPR; OFDM in Wi-Fi, LTE and 5G
Simulating an OFDM link over a frequency-selective channel

units.title: Multiple access: TDMA, FDMA, CDMA and beyond
topics: FDMA, TDMA and their use in 1G and GSM; frame structures
CDMA: spreading codes, processing gain, near-far problem and power control, RAKE receiver; IS-95 and UMTS
OFDMA and SC-FDMA in LTE; NOMA and random access (ALOHA, CSMA) for Wi-Fi and IoT
Capacity comparison of multiple access schemes
Capstone: a MATLAB-style end-to-end simulation of a cellular link with fading, coding, modulation and multiple access

schedule.title: History, architecture and spectrum
schedule.exercise: Write a short timeline from 1G to 5G naming one defining technology change at each generation, and explain why spectrum must be licensed.

tasks.title: Build a timeline table of 1G through 5G listing the defining air interface and data rate of each generation
Draw a cellular network architecture diagram showing a mobile, base station, core network and the handover between two base stations
Compare licensed and unlicensed spectrum bands used in Ghana for three described services, and justify which band suits each

schedule.title: Other wireless systems and the simulation environment
schedule.exercise: Compare satellite, WLAN, WPAN and microwave links for extending coverage to a remote village, and recommend one with reasons.

tasks.title: Compare the coverage and data rate of satellite, WLAN and WPAN links for a described rural scenario, and recommend one
Set up the simulation environment and generate a noisy sine wave signal, then recover its frequency with a Fourier transform
Model a rural coverage scenario in the network simulator comparing a microwave backhaul link with a satellite link on latency

schedule.title: Modulation and link budgets
schedule.exercise: Compute the link budget for a given transmit power, antenna gain and path loss, and determine the margin above the receiver sensitivity.

tasks.title: Plot the constellation diagrams for ASK, FSK, PSK and QAM and compare their bandwidth efficiency for the same data rate
Compute a link budget from transmit power, antenna gain, path loss and noise figure, and determine whether the link closes for a given receiver sensitivity
Pass a digital signal through a raised-cosine pulse shaping filter and show the eye diagram closing as intersymbol interference increases with excess bandwidth

schedule.title: Propagation models
schedule.exercise: Compare the free space, two-ray and log-distance path loss models for the same link distance, and explain why they disagree.

tasks.title: Compute received power at three distances using the free space, two-ray and log-distance path loss models and compare the results
Compute coherence bandwidth and coherence time from given delay spread and Doppler spread, and classify the channel as fast or slow fading
Generate a Rayleigh-faded signal envelope and measure its level crossing rate and average fade duration at a chosen threshold

schedule.title: Wideband channels and fading simulation
schedule.exercise: Classify three described channels as flat or frequency-selective and as slow or fast fading, with the reasoning for each classification.

tasks.title: Model a wideband channel with a tapped delay line and plot its power delay profile from the tap values
Simulate Rayleigh fading with the Jakes model for a given mobile speed and carrier frequency, and classify the resulting channel as flat or frequency selective
Compare a simulated slow fading channel with a fast fading channel at two different mobile speeds and explain the practical effect on a voice call

schedule.title: The cellular concept and capacity
schedule.exercise: Compute the signal-to-interference ratio for a given cluster size, and determine the smallest cluster size that still meets a required ratio.

tasks.title: Compute the reuse distance for a given cell radius and cluster size, and verify it against the formula relating the two
Compute the signal-to-interference ratio for co-channel cells at a given cluster size and determine if it meets a stated quality target
Compare the capacity gain of sectoring and cell splitting on the same coverage area and recommend one approach for a given traffic growth

schedule.title: Handover, power control and cellular design
schedule.exercise: Design a cellular layout for a Ghanaian town given a traffic forecast and coverage target, justifying the cell size and cluster size chosen.

tasks.title: Diagram a handover between two base stations as a mobile moves, marking the point where power control reduces interference to the neighbouring cell
Design a cellular layout for a described Ghanaian town meeting a given traffic forecast and coverage target, and justify the cell count
Simulate a mobile moving between two simulated base stations and verify the handover completes without dropping the active call

schedule.title: Traffic theory and QoS
schedule.exercise: Use the Erlang B formula to compute the number of channels a cell needs for a given offered load and blocking probability target.

tasks.title: Compute offered traffic in erlangs for a cell from a given number of subscribers and average call duration
Use the Erlang B and Erlang C formulas on the same offered load and compare the required channels for a blocked-calls-cleared versus a queued system
Dimension a cell's channels for a target blocking probability under a given traffic forecast, and verify the result against the Erlang B table

schedule.title: Detection and error performance
schedule.exercise: Derive the symbol error probability for BPSK in AWGN at a given signal-to-noise ratio, and compare it with a simulated result.

tasks.title: Implement a correlation receiver for a BPSK signal in noise and show it correctly detects the transmitted bits above a given signal-to-noise ratio
Compute theoretical bit error probability for BPSK, QPSK and 16-QAM at the same signal-to-noise ratio and compare bandwidth versus power efficiency
Compare average bit error rate in a Rayleigh fading channel against an AWGN channel at the same average signal-to-noise ratio and explain the gap

schedule.title: Synchronisation and Monte Carlo simulation
schedule.exercise: Run a Monte Carlo bit error rate simulation for a given modulation and compare the result with the theoretical curve, explaining any gap.

tasks.title: Estimate the timing offset of a received signal against a known reference and show the effect of correcting it on the recovered symbols
Estimate a simple channel's gain from a known pilot sequence and use it to equalise a distorted received signal
Run a Monte Carlo simulation of BPSK bit error rate over a range of signal-to-noise ratios and overlay it on the theoretical curve

schedule.title: Channel capacity and coding
schedule.exercise: Explain, with a diagram, how Viterbi decoding finds the most likely transmitted sequence for a convolutionally coded, noisy received sequence.

tasks.title: Compute Shannon capacity for an AWGN channel and for a fading channel with the same average signal-to-noise ratio, and explain the capacity loss
Encode a bit sequence with a Hamming code, introduce a single-bit error, and show the code detects and corrects it
Encode a bit sequence with a convolutional code and decode a noisy version with the Viterbi algorithm, and compare it with the original sequence
Simulate hybrid ARQ retransmission for a packet corrupted by noise, and measure how many retransmissions are needed before successful decoding

schedule.title: Diversity, MIMO and OFDM
schedule.exercise: Explain how maximal-ratio combining improves on selection diversity for two received copies of the same faded signal.

tasks.title: Simulate selection diversity and maximal-ratio combining over two Rayleigh-faded branches and compare the resulting bit error rate
Simulate a 2 by 2 MIMO spatial multiplexing link and compare its capacity with a single-antenna link at the same signal-to-noise ratio
Simulate an OFDM link with a cyclic prefix over a frequency-selective channel and show it removes intersymbol interference that a single-carrier link would suffer

schedule.title: Multiple access and the capstone link simulation
schedule.exercise: Compare FDMA, TDMA, CDMA and OFDMA for the same number of users and total bandwidth, and justify which access scheme suits a dense urban cell.

tasks.title: Simulate three users sharing a channel with FDMA and TDMA and compare the data rate each user gets under both schemes
Simulate CDMA spreading for two users with different codes and show a RAKE receiver separates them despite sharing the same frequency and time slot
Build an end-to-end simulation of a cellular link combining fading, coding, modulation and a chosen multiple access scheme, and report the resulting bit error rate
